newsitem.title: USA: Algerian Islamic militant vows U.S. hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Algerian Islamic militant vows U.S. hunger strike.

text.p: A leading member of Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front announced from his jail cell on Thursday that he would go on a hunger strike to press his case for political asylum in the United States.

Anwar Haddam, who has been spokesman for the group in Washington, called on the United States either to grant him asylum immediatedly or to turn him over to his foes in Algeria's army-backed government.
"I would prefer to be killed in the hand of the Algerian junta, in my country, than to be held with criminals in the U.S.," he said in an open letter faxed to Reuters.
Calling himself a political prisoner, Haddam said he would begin a hunger strike next Wednesday to protest "the psychological terror I have been put through since my arrest and detention."
Haddam was detained by the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service on Dec. 6 after his "parole" status, letting him stay in the United States legally, expired.

He was among 188 Islamic militants who won seats in Algeria's 430-member legislature in the first round of an election in December 1991. The Algerian army intervened to cancel a runoff in January 1992, blocking a victory by the Salvation Front and setting the stage for civil strife that has killed about 60,000 people.
"The U.S. government is to be held responsible for the consequences of those who took the irresponsible decisions to keep in prison a duly elected political figure," Haddam said in his open letter.

Haddam's asylum case was denied by the INS in October. He is being held at an INS detention facility in Manassas, Virginia, outide Washington. The INS did not immediately return a phone call seeking comment.
